Verified R1-01/02/03/04 additive claim with actual joint faithfulness test
decision: Additive sum (86.5%) was not a valid faithfulness measure on its own — individual-effect sums ignore interference/synergy and can over- or under-count. Actual joint patch of {L9H9,L10H0,L9H6} gives faithfulness 0.8827 (clean 2.7633, corrupted -3.5601, patched 2.0216), beats random control (mean 0.0275, std 0.058, 100th percentile) — clears 0.7 target. score_vs_truth: precision 1.0, recall 0.1154 (3/26), f1 0.2069; name_mover recall 1.0 but backup_name_mover, s_inhibition, duplicate/induction/previous-token all 0% recall. SURPRISE: additive estimate happened to undershoot the true joint effect here (86.5% vs 88.3%), implying mild positive synergy rather than overlap/double-counting — breaks the assumption that summing independent single-head patches necessarily overstates a joint effect; also S-inhibition path-patch to these receivers was negligible (<0.1%), so the high faithfulness is carried entirely by 3 name-mover heads, not a complete IOI circuit.
